title: Fixed-embedding Mirror adapter decoder vs HyperFormer-style hypernetwork
hypothesis: With identical fixed task-factor embeddings and a shared frozen backbone/adapter basis, a structured Mirror decoder can generate useful adapters for held-out task-factor combinations with lower full inference bytes than a generic HyperFormer-style decoder, and can beat simple linear/additive decoders when task variation is factor-aligned.
physical_object: One frozen shared feature backbone plus a shared adapter-atom basis at its output projection.
mirror_coordinate: For task factors (a,b), m(a,b)=((E_A[a] P_A) elementwise-multiplied by (E_B[b] P_B)) Q, decoded to coefficients over shared adapter atoms.
logical_multiplicity: Generated task adapters for a 4×4 task-factor grid, including four held-out factor pairs.

random_selection.selection_rule: registry rows priority=P0 AND status=UNTESTED; exclude every ID with any remote research/ma-* branch; numeric ID order

conditioning_embeddings: Fixed E_A and E_B tables generated once per world, identical and frozen across all decoder methods; included in every applicable serialized inference payload. No decoder may train or replace these conditioning embeddings.
controls: Frozen shared backbone with no adapter
Native HyperFormer-style generic MLP hypernetwork emitting coefficients over the same shared adapter atoms
Additive factor decoder (E_A P_A + E_B P_B) over the same atoms
Flat learned coefficient per seen task
Mirror decoder plus per-task private coefficient residual
Independent full adapter matrix per seen task as upper control

development.selection_metric: alpha=1 held-out task NMSE plus fixed byte/control gates; inspect the full alpha frontier but do not select on fresh
development.allowed_tuning: Mirror/additive latent rank in {2,4,8}; decoder optimizer, architecture and update count fixed.

fresh.all_methods: same methods and rank selected on development; no exclusions after fresh access

data.generator: Synthetic task-conditioned regression over a shared frozen MLP feature model. The target adapter code is alpha*view_code(a,b)+(1-alpha)*private_code(task). view_code is generated from products of two latent projections of fixed factor embeddings; private_code is independent per task.
data.factor_grid: 4×4 tasks; pairs (0,0),(1,2),(2,3),(3,1) held out from decoder fitting; every factor value remains represented in training tasks.
data.base_pretraining: 500 Adam updates on a task-agnostic common teacher per world, then backbone frozen before adapter decoder comparison.
data.reproducibility_note: Set torch seed before constructing each base model so weight and bias initialization are deterministic; final development replay must match.

paid_objects: flat task coefficient table or private residual where present

compute.report_active_compute_proxy: decoder-generation MACs per task, adapter-application MACs per example, and 3× forward proxy for training
compute.runtime: measure per-task decoder generation separately from applying generated adapters over evaluation examples; count generated code cache bytes as transient state

development_gate: At alpha=1 on both development worlds, at least one rank must satisfy: Mirror seen and held-out NMSE <=1.10x generic HyperFormer; Mirror held-out NMSE <=0.80x the best of linear and additive simple controls; full serialized Mirror payload <=0.80x HyperFormer payload. If none pass, record FAIL and do not open fresh.
success_gate: After passing the development gate and freezing the smallest passing rank, all three fresh worlds at alpha=1 meet the same quality and storage gates. Report the full alpha=0..1 shared/private frontier; alpha=0 is a private-variation boundary, not a required Mirror pass.
failure_gate: No development rank passes the aligned alpha=1 gate, or any fresh world fails the frozen aligned gate. Never tune on fresh worlds.
boundaries: Synthetic decoder mechanism screen, not a language/GLUE benchmark and not a reproduction of the full HyperFormer++ paper.
All decoder methods receive identical fixed E_A/E_B conditioning embeddings.
The shared frozen backbone and adapter atoms are common across methods and their complete bytes are charged.
Alpha=0 private codes are independent across tasks; unseen private task behavior is not predictable without private state.
No capacity claim: fixed 300 decoder updates.
